predeclaredReadingRules: PASSED: the cell now clears the grader. Because the cell passed once in 27 prior attempts, a pass is consistent with the change having helped and also consistent with variance; it is reported as a signal, never as a measured effect size, and it changes no rate anywhere.

FAILED but the evidence shows unbuffered output, a fault handler, or an abandoned ctypes route: the statements changed this cell's behaviour without changing its verdict. That is the sharpest available reading and is reported as such.

FAILED with the same shape as the baseline (ctypes direct call into Debian lapack, five or more 139s, zero-byte stdout, no unbuffered output): the statements did not change this cell's route, which is evidence against the fix's premise rather than for it.
ERROR or verdict-less: reported as a mechanical attribution (transport seconds, timeout, budget) and never counted as a model failure, exactly as the full-run records do.
In every case, this cell's outcome is compared only against its own baseline cell in 40823203153, never against any other cell and never against a full-run rate.
specificQuestionsToAnswer: Does the model read the 128+N statement and act on it, or does it keep treating 139 as an opaque failure?

Does it use `python -u`, `PYTHONUNBUFFERED`, or `faulthandler` when probing the crash, given the description now names the first two? Baseline used `faulthandler` once and never used unbuffered output.
Does it stop trying to call `dgeev_` through ctypes on the Debian library, or does it repeat that route?
How many real segfaults (exitCode 139, deduplicated by callId) occur, against the baseline's 5 of 31 calls?

knownRisks.singleAttempt: One attempt on a cell that has passed once in 27 tries: the arm can show behaviour, not an effect size.
knownRisks.firstRunOfThisCandidateOnThisCell: 88fddc535 has never run this cell. Its only execution evidence is the regex-log smoke, which does not exercise native debugging.
knownRisks.notAFullRun: If the value of also knowing whether the other 29 cells were perturbed matters later, that question needs its own full arm; this one cannot answer it and does not pretend to.
knownRisks.cancelledPredecessor: Run 40852900814 (30 cells, same candidate) was cancelled before it produced a complete corpus. It is not a reading of anything, no cell of it is cited as a verdict, and its own record must say so.

plannedChecks: Read the cell's own evidence and artifacts: disposition, durationMs, modelCallCount, deduplicated segfault count, whether unbuffered output or a fault handler appears, whether the ctypes route was abandoned, and the mechanical cause of a non-pass. Then read its model.patch and verifier output only if the disposition is passed, to name what satisfied the grader. Record the reading beside the baseline in a .md under docs/benchmarks/history/frontier-harness; never write an .official.json and never touch the baseline record.
